Weng.Modeler
Class Solver

java.lang.Object
  |
  +--Weng.Modeler.Solver
public class Solver
extends java.lang.Object

Use this singleton class to find solutions to geoemtric problems such as entity intersections and tangencies. NOTE: All arc solutions are xy planar, requiring all input to be xy coplanar.

With regards to arc direction, it suggested that you use the constants Const.CCW and Const.CW that are defined in Weng.System.Const. Otherwise, arc direction follows protractor convention (+) CCW / (-) CW.

ArcSER

public static boolean ArcSER(Point ps,
                             Point pe,
                             double radius,
                             int dir,
                             boolean big,

Finds the center point of an arc given its start point, end point, radius, direction and an indication (big) of the desired solution. In most cases, big should be set to false.

Parameters:
ps - the start point of the arc
pe - the end point of the arc
radius - the radius of the arc
dir - the arcs direction
big - (true) calculates the center based on an arc having an included greater than 180 degrees / (false) calculates the center based on an arc having an included angle smaller than 180 degrees.
pc - the resulting center point of the arc
Returns:
(false) no solution

                        DbCurve tanCurveB,
                        double radius,
                        int dir,
                        boolean big,
                        Point hintA,
                        Point hintB)
Finds the arc having the specified radius and direction, that is tangent to given curves.
Parameters:
tanCurveA - first known reference curve
tanCurveB - second known reference curve
radius - known radius if resulting arc
dir - known direction of resulting arc
big - (true) result >= 180 degrees, (false) result <= 180 degrees
hintA - a hint point on tanCurveA indicating the general location where the the resulting arc should contact tanCurveA.
hintB - a hint point on tanCurveB indicating the general location where the the resulting arc should contact tanCurveB.
Returns:
(null) no solution

ArcPAL

public static Arc ArcPAL(Point pt,
                         Arc circle,
                         Line line,
                         Point hint)
Finds the circle that runs through a known point and that is tangent to a line and another circle.
Parameters:
pt - the known point through which the result must run
circle - the known circle to which the result must be tangent
line - the known line to which the result must be tangent
hint - a point on the known circle indicating the approximate tangent location of the result circle. As there can be up to four solutions, the hint point is used as selection criteria.
Returns:
(null) no solution, (otherwise) an arc that satisfies the criteria and whose start point is the tangent point to the known circle.

ClosestPt

public static Point ClosestPt(DbCurve curve,
                              Point pt,
                              boolean onseg)
Finds the point on the reference curve that is closest to the reference point. NOTE: This method finds the 2D solution. It assumes the reference point is in the same workplane as the reference curve. Also, the Z ordinate of the the solution is returned as the Z ordinate of the reference point.
Parameters:
curve - the reference curve
pt - the reference point
onseg - (true) finds a solution in the bounded curve / (false) finds a solution on the unbounded curve.
Returns:
the closest point on the reference curve

Chamfer

public static boolean Chamfer(DbCurve curveA,
                              DbCurve curveB,
                              double angle,
                              double offset,
                              boolean onseg,
                              Point ps,
                              Point pe,
                              boolean[] solnEnds)
Calculates the parameters of a chamfer.
Parameters:
curveA - the first curve to consider
curveB - the second curve to consider
angle - the angle of the chamfer relative to the first curve (radians)
offset - ???
onseg - (true) finds solutions on the bounded portions of the curves / (false) allows solutions on the unbounded portions of the curves
ps - the resulting start point of the chamfer
pe - the resulting end point of the chamfer
solnEnds - a two element array indicating which ends of the curves the solutions lay on, where (solnEnds[0]) represents the solution for the first curve and (solnEnds[1]) represents the solution for the second curve. A value of (true) indicates the solution is near the end of a curve and a value of (false) indicates the solution is near the start of a curve.
Returns:
(false) indicates failure

Blend

public static Arc Blend(DbCurve curveA,
                        DbCurve curveB,
                        double radius,
                        int dir,
                        double tol)
Finds the blending arc between two curve entities whose end points are within proximity of each other. This method is particularly useful for curves that have been 'chained' into a profile.
Parameters:
curveA - the first curve to consider
curveB - the second curve to consider
radius - the radius of the blending arc
dir - the direction of the blending arc
tol - the tolerance by which 'proximity' of curve end points is determined
Returns:
(null) indicates no solution / (else) the blending arc
